fact_en: The cricket is a nocturnal insect that chirps at night by rubbing its wings together.
fact_bis: Ang kagiw usa ka nokturnal nga insekto nga mohuni sa gabii pinaagi sa pagkiskis sa iyang mga pako.

findings.note: EN "The cricket is a nocturnal insect that chirps at night..." -> BIS "Ang KAGIW usa ka nokturnal nga insekto nga mohuni sa gabii...". 'Kagiw' is to flee/evacuate, not an insect; the corpus names the cricket 'kuliglig' in 44 cards, including this card's own title_bis. The body therefore names a non-animal as the subject (only the title hints at kuliglig).

fact_en: The Philippines has a warm, rainy climate all year, so spices like ginger, chili, lemongrass, and garlic grow easily here!
fact_bis: Ang Pilipinas adunay init ug ulanon nga klima sa tibuok tuig, mao nga sayon motubo dinhi ang mga panakot sama sa luya, sili, tanglad, ug ahos!

findings.note: title_bis "Reklamo Klima INIT" for "Spices in Warm Climates": "reklamo" means complaint and has nothing to do with the card; the word for spices (panakot) is dropped entirely, and "INIT" is shouted in caps. The title names a different thing than the card. Body is correct.

fact_en:
Why is no fingerprint the same?

The skin on your fingertips has one-of-a-kind patterns called fingerprints — no two people in the world have the same ones!
fact_bis:
Nganong walay parehas nga fingerprint?

Ang panit sa tumoy sa imong mga tudlo adunay talagsaon nga marka nga gitawag og fingerprint — walay duha ka tawo nga managsama!

findings.note: title_bis "Laing Prints Titi" for "Unique Fingerprint Patterns": the Cebuano title never says finger/tudlo — "titi" is not the word for finger or toe, and across Filipino languages it reads as the vulgar term for penis. On a grade-5 card the title names a different (and unsafe) body part; only the body restores "tumoy sa imong mga tudlo". Same generator error recurs in ffct-00424 ("Prints sa Titi ug Palad", EN toes) and ffct-00131 ("Titi sa Tiil sa Alibangbang", EN tasting feet), so the grep is worth running.

fact_en: A whale can hold its breath and dive deep for many minutes before coming back up to breathe air!
fact_bis: Ang balyena makapugong sa iyang ginhawa ug molusong og lawom sulod sa daghang minuto ayha motungha aron makaginhawa!

findings.note: title_bis "Balyena Ginhawa Lango" for "Whales Hold Breath Dive": "lango" means dizzy/stupefied/drunk, not dive (body correctly uses "molusong og lawom"). Reads as a fainting whale; the diving fact is absent from the title. Lower severity than the others — likely a truncation of "langoy" — but it is a real wrong word in the title.

fact_en: In many places, including the Philippines, people boil certain tree barks to make a drink used as traditional medicine.
fact_bis: Sa daghang dapit, lakip ang Pilipinas, adunay mga tawo nga nagalunod og panit sa kahoy aron himoong tradisyonal nga tambal nga ilimnon.

findings.note: English: 'people BOIL certain tree barks to make a drink used as traditional medicine.' Cebuano: 'nagalunod og panit sa kahoy' — lunod means to sink/submerge/drown, not to boil, so the Cebuano says people SOAK (or drown) bark rather than boil it, and nothing in the card restores the boiling. The card is a single sentence whose whole content is the preparation method, so the method fact is lost. Corpus-wide this translator otherwise renders boil correctly as pabukal/pabukalon (ffct-02282, ffct-01030, ffct-04385) or lat-an/gilat-an (ffct-01940 'gilat-an ang gamot sa kugon', ffct-01223, ffct-02355); 'lunod' in its 107 other corpus occurrences always means submerged/drowned, so this one is the outlier.

fact_en: Toads have dry, bumpy skin and live mostly on land, unlike smooth, water-loving frogs.
fact_bis: Ang mga bakulaw adunay uga ug bukol-bukol nga panit ug kasagaran nagpuyo sa yuta, dili sama sa hapsay ug tubig-tubig nga mga baki.

findings.note: Title 'Bakulaw vs Baki' and body 'Ang mga bakulaw adunay uga ug bukol-bukol nga panit...' use bakulaw for TOAD. In standard Cebuano bakulaw is a large ape/monkey (a big hairy creature), not an amphibian, and the card never corrects it — a child reads that 'bakulaw' (an ape) has dry bumpy skin and lives on land, unlike frogs. Corpus-internal evidence supports the swap being wrong: the same corpus renders toad as baki (ffct-00232 'Ang baki o toad'), kamprag (ffct-00641), kabkab (ffct-06098, ffct-14393), kabakaba (ffct-06020), or just 'toad' (ffct-11999). bakulaw-for-toad occurs only 3x corpus-wide (ffct-02488, ffct-05158, ffct-05377), so the grep is cheap. Confidence moderate, not certain — worth one native-speaker check before mass-editing.

fact_en: Macaques make different calls and sounds to warn the rest of their group whenever danger is near.
fact_bis: Ang mga unggoy mohimo og lain-laing tawag o tingog aron pasidan-an ang ilang mga kauban kon adunay nagkaduol nga kakuyaw.

findings.note: Lower severity, title-only: title_bis 'Babala sa Macaque sa Kapeckan' contains 'Kapeckan', which is not a Cebuano word — 'ck' is not even native Cebuano orthography; the intended sense is danger (kakuyaw/katalagman/kapeligrohan), which the body does supply ('kon adunay nagkaduol nga kakuyaw'), so the FACT is recoverable and this is not a meaning reversal. Flagged because it is a user-visible garbled title token, not dialect or register, and it recurs 7x corpus-wide as the house rendering of 'danger' (ffct-06876, ffct-13041, ffct-15779, ffct-27838, ffct-29330, ffct-29335) — one grep fixes all of them. Treat as a corpus-wide typo sweep, not a per-card fact defect.

fact_en:
Why do deep wounds leave a scar?

A deep wound can leave a scar because the new tissue that fills it in isn't exactly the same as your original skin.
fact_bis:
Ngano nga adunay peklat sa lawom nga samad?

Kon lawom ang samad, usahay mabilin kini og peklat tungod kay ang bag-ong unod nga mopuno niini dili parehas sa orihinal nga panit.

findings.note: title_bis "Peke sa Lawom nga Samad" = "fake of the deep wound". peke means counterfeit/fake everywhere else in the corpus (ffct-13448 butterfly fake head, ffct-17499, ffct-24018); the word for scar is peklat, which the body uses. Same title swap at ffct-06230 ("Deep Wounds Leave Scars" -> "Lawom nga Samad Peke"), so it is a repeated defect, not a one-off typo.

fact_en:
Is there a real cure for the common cold?

No! There's no direct cure for the common cold. Medicine only helps you feel better while your own body heals itself.
fact_bis:
Naa bay tinuod nga tambal sa sip-on?

Wala! Walay direktang tambal sa komon nga sip-on. Ang tambal makatabang lang aron mogaan ang bati samtang ang imong lawas mismo ang nag-ayo.

findings.note: title_bis "Walay Tambal sa Ubo" = "no cure for the cough"; EN and the BIS body are about the common cold (sip-on). Cough and cold are different illnesses to a grade-5 reader. Same swap recurs at ffct-02131 ("Colds Clear in a Week" -> "Ubo Gikan sa Pito ka Adlaw") and ffct-02368, while ffct-00027 gets it right with sip-on.

fact_en: Cotyledons are the seed leaves that store food to feed a young seedling — until it grows big enough to make its own food through photosynthesis.
fact_bis: Ang cotyledon mao ang seed leaf sa liso nga adunay tinipigan nga pagkaon aron pakan-on ang bag-ong salingsing — hangtod nga makahimo na kini og kaugalingong pagkaon pinaagi sa photosynthesis.

findings.note: title_bis "Cotyledon Pagkaon sa Lumot" = "Cotyledon, food of the moss/algae". EN title is "Cotyledons Feed Seedlings"; lumot is used ~150x in the corpus for algae/moss, and every other seedling card uses semilya (ffct-00394, ffct-01465, ffct-03155). The title names a different organism — cotyledons do not feed algae.

fact_en: The bladder stretches and grows bigger as it fills up with urine, just like a balloon filling with water.
fact_bis: Ang pantog moluag ug modako samtang mapuno sa ihi, sama sa lobo nga gipuno og tubig.

findings.note: title_bis "Nagtapak nga Pantog" for "Bladder Stretches as It Fills" — tapak means to patch/step on, not to stretch or expand; the body correctly says "moluag ug modako". Title-only, lower confidence than the rows above, but it recurs as the corpus's stock title word for expand (ffct-19997 air in balloons, ffct-20393 metal bridges, ffct-21565 ice), so one grep settles four titles at once.

fact_en:
Why chew your food well?

If you swallow before your molars grind the food small, you might choke! That's why chewing properly really matters.
fact_bis:
Nganong kinahanglan mo-usap og maayo?

Kon tunlon nimo sa dili pa mapino sa bag-ang ang pagkaon, basin mahurot ka! Mao nga importante ang husto nga pag-usap.

findings.note: EN warns "you might choke" if you swallow before molars grind food. BIS says "basin mahurot ka" — mahurot = to be used up/run out (the corpus uses it that way in ~20 other cards: mahurot ang isda, mahurot ang oxygen). The choking danger, which is the whole point of the card, is never stated; the Cebuano reads as "you might get used up". Cebuano for choking exists and is used elsewhere (ffct-07198: "Nabilaw"). Same card also has title_bis "Maayong Ngisi sa Bagang" — ngisi = grin, not chew (grep pair chew->ngisi also hits ffct-07198).
